title: Food-order refund via a "refund helper" app vs. refund credited to the in-app wallet
summary: The recipient reported a missing item in a KhanaGo food order through the app an hour ago. A caller from "KhanaGo support" phones back. In the legitimate case, the agent apologises, credits the refund to the recipient's KhanaGo wallet during the call, and asks them to check the wallet in the app. In the fraud case, the caller says refunds are now processed through a separate "refund helper" app, sends a download link, and tells the recipient to install it and allow the permissions it asks for. This differs from `ec_13` in the mechanism (installing an app from a link, rather than turning on screen sharing) and the setting (a one-off food refund, rather than a recurring subscription). Both cases involve opening an app to see the refund.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a KhanaGo customer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: The recipient really did raise a complaint in the app; the complaint reference is [TICKET_ID].
Both callers quote the complaint reference and the missing item.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller tells the recipient to install an app from a link they send, and to allow its permissions, in order to receive a refund. Apps pushed by callers can take over the device or read messages; a genuine refund needs no extra software.
fraud.caller_objective: Get a remote-access or message-reading app installed, then use it to move money.
stable_facts: The link arrives by SMS as https://khanago-refund.invalid/helper.
The caller says the KhanaGo app "cannot process refunds under ₹[AMOUNT_13] directly".
The caller says to "allow all permissions" so the refund can be "verified".

legitimate.label_rationale: The agent credits the refund to the KhanaGo wallet from their side. The recipient only opens the app they already have to see the credit.
legitimate.caller_objective: Close the complaint with a refund and an apology.
stable_facts: The refund is credited to the KhanaGo wallet during the call; the recipient can move it to the original PaySetu account from the wallet screen if they prefer.
A notification from the KhanaGo app confirms the credit.
The agent closes the complaint and asks if anything else is wrong with the order.

clarifying.legitimate: Asks how long the bank transfer from the wallet takes

resistant.fraud: Says they will take the refund as wallet credit in the KhanaGo app instead
resistant.legitimate: Says they want the money in their bank, not the wallet

suspicious.fraud: Says they will not install anything from a link

fraud: caller insists the refund will lapse and recipient hangs up
legitimate: agent suggests checking the complaint status in the app's Help section when suspicious.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may resend the link, reassure that the app is "official", or add a deadline. They must not switch to asking for card details, OTPs, collect requests, or screen sharing. The legitimate agent must not send any link or ask the recipient to install or allow anything.

must_preserve: complaint reference and refund amount in both cases
wallet credit in the existing app in _L
must_not_emit: names of real remote-access or screen-sharing apps
permission names from real phone systems

ambiguities: Opening an app is not evidence: the legitimate recipient also opens an app. The label rests on installing new software from a caller's link.
Knowing the complaint reference does not make a caller genuine; both callers know it.
If the fraud caller only sends a link without telling the recipient to install it, the prefix is not eligible.

evidence_references.claim: Do not install screen-sharing or SMS-forwarding apps at an unknown person's request (C09)
Impersonating callers may ask you to download an app that steals data; hang up (CE18)
A major marketplace states it will never ask customers to install software for support (CE14)
Refund scams ask victims to install remote-access apps (CE22)
